source.state: CI follow-up: active-time wake fix and acknowledged native touch regression

affectedBrowserCases.command: COMPATIBILITY_TEST_PORT=5215 npm run test:e2e:compatibility --prefix client -- crystal-dormancy.spec.js

findings: Five wake assertions exceeded their unchanged deadline because active deltas above 100ms were discarded.
One native Android swipe returned without panel scrolling; explicit acknowledged native touch events now prove hit target, cancellation and scrolling.

coverage: Full finite active elapsed time, quiet/wake boundary splitting, low-FPS and timestep-consistency regressions
Existing hidden and first-resumed-frame exclusions remain tested
Actual simulation/shader clock freeze, light dimming, keyboard, pointer cancellation, focus loss and touch recovery
Native touch press/move/end requires actual canvas hit, pointer cancellation and more than 20px of native scrolling
limitations: The 29 local affected cases are a subset of the full 124-case hosted matrix. GitHub Actions evaluates that complete matrix on each pushed follow-up.
Local device emulation is not physical iPhone or Android testing. Manual physical-phone feedback remains separate.
The separate hardware capture qualifies only the recorded Apple M3 Max and viewport; rAF is not proof of presentation or GPU execution time.
